scenes.name: hook
scenes.text: People say dark mode saves battery. Sometimes it does, sometimes it barely matters. It depends on your screen.

scenes.name: oled
scenes.text: In an OLED screen, every pixel makes its own light. A black pixel is simply switched off, using almost no power.

scenes.name: lcd
scenes.text: An LCD screen has one backlight behind all the pixels, always on. Black pixels just block that light, so it still uses power.

scenes.name: bright
scenes.text: On OLED phones, studies found dark mode saves the most at high brightness. At normal indoor brightness, the savings are much smaller.

scenes.name: content
scenes.text: It only helps where the screen is actually dark. Bright photos and videos use the same power either way.

scenes.name: check
scenes.text: Many flagship and mid range phones today use OLED or AMOLED. Many budget phones still use LCD.

scenes.name: eyes
scenes.text: Battery aside, many people simply find dark mode easier on the eyes at night. Pick what feels comfortable.

scenes.name: outro
scenes.text: OLED, pixels off, brightness, content. It depends. Follow for more on how things really work.
